dicas.texto: Você está no caminho certo! Se cada copo inteiro tem 4 partes de um quarto, quantas partes de um quarto existem em 2 copos inteiros?
Tente multiplicar a parte inteira (2) pelo denominador (4) e depois somar com o numerador da fração (3) para encontrar o total de quartos.
Você tem 8 quartos nos dois copos inteiros. Agora, adicione os 3 quartos que sobraram. Qual o total de quartos?
Você tem 8/4 + 3/4. Somando os numeradores, você chega no valor final que deve colocar na caixa de cima, mantendo o denominador 4 embaixo.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem?" com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); reta numérica de 0 a 3 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 4 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

campo: denominador da parte fracionária do número misto ("-" quando não há)
reta numérica; o aluno adiciona um ponto (marca a posição da fração)
grupo com m1/m2/m3, exibido depois de Convert

campo numérico da caixa de cima da fração (numerador)
campo numérico: parte inteira do número misto

dicas.texto: Count the completely filled cups first, then identify the fraction of the additional cup.
Write the whole-number part first and place the numerator and denominator of the remaining fraction in their matching fields.
The whole-number part is the number of full cups, and the remaining part has three equal pieces with four pieces in the whole.
Set the whole-number field to the number of full cups, the numerator field to the filled pieces, and the denominator field to the total equal pieces.
An improper fraction expresses the entire amount using equal fractional parts instead of separating full cups from the remaining part.
Multiply the whole-number part by the denominator, add the numerator, and keep the denominator unchanged.
Use the two full groups of fourths and then add the three fourths that remain.
Complete the conversion by combining the fourths from the full cups with the three additional fourths, while keeping fourths as the unit.
The numerator tells how many fractional parts are present altogether.
Convert each full cup into fourths, then add the three fourths from the remaining cup.
Each of the two full cups contains four fourths. Combine those fourths with the three additional fourths.
Multiply the whole-number part by four and add three; enter that total in the top field.
The denominator names the size of the equal fractional parts.
Look at how many equal parts make one whole cup.
The remaining cup is divided into four equal parts, and the conversion keeps that same denominator.
Enter the number of equal parts in one whole cup in the lower field.
First locate the whole-number interval containing the amount, then locate the fractional part within that interval.
Start at 2 and divide the distance to 3 into four equal intervals.
Move three equal intervals to the right from 2, stopping one interval before 3.
Place the point at the third quarter mark after 2, using the fourth quarter as the distance unit.
Before finishing, check that the fraction and the point describe the same amount of juice.
Verify the numerator, denominator, and location of the point in that order.
The numerator should count all fourths, the denominator should name fourths, and the point should lie between 2 and 3.
Confirm that the point is three quarter-intervals after 2 and that the fraction fields use the same fourths, then submit the completed representation.

exercicio.statement:
Every morning, Lili's mother prepares a pitcher of tomato juice for Lili and her sister. One morning, Lili's mother made the pitcher a bit too large; it completely filled Lili's cup, her sister's up, and the left over filled about 3/4 of a third cup. Show the number of cups of tomato juice Lili's mother prepared that morning on the number line.
What is the fraction in the problem?

Mark 2 3/4 on the number line from 0 to 3.
After checking the fraction and point, click Done.

hints.message: An improper fraction expresses the entire amount using equal fractional parts instead of separating full cups from the remaining part.
Multiply the whole-number part by the denominator, add the numerator, and keep the denominator unchanged.
Use the two full groups of fourths and then add the three fourths that remain.
Complete the conversion by combining the fourths from the full cups with the three additional fourths, while keeping fourths as the unit.

hints.message: The numerator tells how many fractional parts are present altogether.
Convert each full cup into fourths, then add the three fourths from the remaining cup.
Each of the two full cups contains four fourths. Combine those fourths with the three additional fourths.
Multiply the whole-number part by four and add three; enter that total in the top field.

Move three equal intervals to the right from 2, stopping one interval before 3.

Verify the numerator, denominator, and location of the point in that order.

Confirm that the point is three quarter-intervals after 2 and that the fraction fields use the same fourths, then submit the completed representation.
